body: This rule is just a nightmare. :) Might need to look at refactoring it somehow.

Seems to fail also with a plain import (no renaming):

``` js
import Network from "js/network";
```

```
test.js
  1:7  error  "Network" used outside of binding context  block-scoped-var

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```
Yes, this rule doesn't work with import.

Not at all :) It still causes the same errors in this case:

``` javascript
export createRedux from './createRedux';
...
```

Which generates follow output:

```
src/index.js
  2:7  error  "createRedux" used outside of binding context         block-scoped-var
...
```

AFAIK TC39 decided not to support this syntax after all.
Does `export { default as createRedux } from './createRedux` work as intended?

@gaearon it doesn't work too:

``` javascript
export {default as createRedux} from './createRedux';
...
```

```
src/index.js
  2:8   error  "default" used outside of binding context             block-scoped-var
```

I think autocompletion has accidentally completed a wrong Denis.
